description: Put a QUESTION OF YOUR OWN to a named person — the owner, a colleague — about the nodes it concerns, when no detected gap raised it: which foundations they take as given, what a word means here, whether to keep a proof's last step. `asked_of` (a Contributor) and `about` (one or more node ids) are required, and each is checked before anything is written. It then waits like any question put to a person: listed with `origin: asker`, counted by loop_status, and listed for that person by loop_status(contributor_id) until they reply, with whoever replied recorded. Its wording never changes; the same id again re-puts it. Never park one as a Decision with no edges. Ask for this to ask the owner something yourself and keep the question in the design.

about.description:
The nodes it is about, by id — at least one. Each is linked
(ASKS_ABOUT), so the person opens what the question concerns and the
question is found from it. An id the design does not hold is refused.

asked_at.description: When it was put, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

asked_of.description:
The Contributor it is put to (`who:jane`). Required, and refused unless
it names a Contributor.

batch.description:
The batch it travels in, as you name it (`round-2`); numbered in the
order put.

context_setter.description: One or two sentences that place the person back in the design.

echo.description: What the reply carries. `receipt` (the default) names the node, echoes each stored value of at most 200 characters, gives longer ones by size, and names the snapshot that keeps anything a revise replaced. `node` returns the whole stored node and every prior value.

id.description:
Its id. Omitted, one is derived from the wording
(`question:asked-<words>-<hash>`). The same id again re-puts the same
question; different wording under it is refused.

question.description:
The question, in the words the person will read. It never changes once
asked: its answer is given to these words.

name: ask_question
title: Ask a Question of Your Own
